correctness.rationale: Independent geometric and arithmetic reconstruction matches all 29 marked pairs and all eleven rows. Write the sextic as G(X²,Y²,Z²), where G is a plane cubic. In coordinates R=U−W, S=V−W its equation is d_h(R,S)+(a+b+3)(R²−RS+S²)W, with d(r)=r³+ar²+br+1 the dehomogenization of d_h. A node at [1:1:1] needs a+b+3 nonzero; the cubic is geometrically irreducible exactly when gcd(d,r²−r+1)=1 in this case (homogeneous infinity is not a common root). An irreducible cubic with this ordinary node has no further geometric singularities. On the torus squaring is étale; on the axes the only additional obstruction is a repeated root of the binary cubic d_h on the original coordinate line, tested by gcd(d,d′). No coordinate vertex lies on the sextic. The four lifted nodes are split since −3 is a square in F7. Bézout excludes reducibility of the sextic with only four ordinary double points (distinct positive-degree components of total degree six require at least five transverse pair intersections; repeated components are impossible); the normalized genus is 6. Conversely geometric integrality of the sextic implies that of its cubic image and the node/axis tests are necessary. For the quotient by sign changes in X and Y the cubic normalization is rational, and the cyclic permutation conjugates the three intermediate involutions over F7. The three nontrivial character summands for this Klein four action on the Jacobian give three copies up to isogeny of one intermediate-quotient Jacobian. Parametrizing the cubic by R/S=r gives V/W=(d−(a+b+3)(r²−r+1))/d; extracting its square root and substituting u=1/r gives precisely the stated genus-two equation. The independent run counted the plane models directly over both fields, corrected the four nodes, and checked 3#D−2(q+1) separately by square-class point counts. Newton identities give the reported t,s; the degree of the numerator mod 7 is 3 only at (5,5) and 6 otherwise. The largest N1 is 26 exactly at (0,3) and (3,0).
residual_risks: The enumeration is confined to ordered marked coefficients over F7. The Weil numerator does not classify the curves up to isomorphism or determine their Cartier a-numbers.

value.rationale: The complete parameter space of a standard nodal genus-six family over the specified small field is a natural finite domain, rather than an individual cherry-picked curve. The exact table links the geometric admissibility condition to isogeny types, exhibits a single nonordinary parameter, and separates the marked parameters attaining the point extremum. It is reusable exact test data for varying characteristic or comparing genus-six Jacobians; no moduli classification is asserted.
residual_risks: No evidence of a uniform stratification across fields or finer invariants of the exceptional Jacobian.
